financialCondition.headline: This franchisor has negative net worth (about $360K in the red) — it owes more than it owns — though the trend isn't worsening. Understand what's funding the gap before you commit.
financialCondition.context: Worth perspective: the auditor issued a clean (unmodified) opinion and did not raise going-concern doubt; revenue is growing; the business is profitable. Note what this is and is not: the negative net worth sits alongside positive net income of $11K, so the balance sheet reflects how this business was financed rather than how it trades. Ask what created the gap — a recapitalization, distributions to the owner, or accumulated losses from earlier years — because those carry very different consequences for a franchisee.
body: What we found (2025, audited by Kezos & Dunlavy): Net income of $11K on $3.54M of revenue — roughly 1.0x spent per $1 earned. Negative net worth (a members'/stockholders' deficit) of $360K. Total liabilities are about 1.1x total assets. Cash of $213K against $924K of obligations due within a year (a current ratio of 1.25). Note: about 20% of those liabilities is deferred revenue — prepaid franchise fees the company owes as future services, not borrowed money. Netting it out, liabilities are still about 0.9x assets.

Why it matters to you: field support, training, technology, and marketing come out of the franchisor's budget. If outside funding slows, those are the first things to get cut. There is no parent guarantee of performance in this FDD, so Cabinet IQ Holdings, LLC is not contractually obligated to keep funding the franchisor or backing its commitments to you.

Verify before you commit: ask for the most recent interim (unaudited) financials and the current-year funding plan; ask whether the parent will sign a guarantee of performance; and cross-check Item 20 — unit closures, transfers, and terminations are the operational tell that corroborates financial stress.
aggravators: negative net worth — it owes more than it owns
no parent guarantee backing the franchisor's obligations to you
mitigants: the auditor issued a clean (unmodified) opinion and did not raise going-concern doubt
